history.hypothesis: this gate, not the bot's inability to kill, is what caps every run at the bottom of the XP ladder, and lowering it will raise mean progression because XP is the scored term. NetHack awards xp = 1 + mlevel * mlet for a kill (src/monst.c), and experience_level 8 costs 20+40+80+160+320+640+1280 = 2540 points. The population of dlvl 1 is overwhelmingly level-0: grid bug, goblin, jackal, newt, kobold, bat, lichen and sewer rat are all worth exactly 1 xp. So this gate demanded ~2540 kills out of the only monsters that exist on the level the bot starts on -- ~10^5 turns at the measured ~1 kill per 60 turns, and it exhausts the level long before that. One level down, the same kills are worth 16 (orc) to 117 (iguana), so descending multiplies xp per kill by one to two orders of magnitude. Descending early is also near-free for the score: progression is a running max, so a seed that already banked xp keeps it, and Dlvl:2-5 (0.0154-0.0265) sit between Xp:2 and Xp:5, so a shallower-but-alive run cannot score much below the 2540-point grind it replaces. Level 4 is ~60 xp banked -- roughly a dozen real kills, enough that the character has proved it can win a fight, and ~2% of what level 8 demanded. It is a guess at the safest useful bar, not a tuned constant: what the number cannot be is 8.
